references.text: Tells about Judah's sons Er and Onan, and their death in the land of Canaan.
Describes the birth of Perez and Zerah, the twin sons of Judah and Tamar.
A near parallel listing Judah's sons, mentioning the deaths of Er and Onan in Canaan, and the sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
Genealogy of Judah's descendants: Perez and Zerah as sons of Tamar (v.4), and Hezron and Hamul as sons of Perez (v.5).
Lists descendants of Judah, with Perez mentioned as the patriarch.
The lineage of Perez through Hezron, relevant to the mention of Perez's sons in this verse.
Confirms the story of Er and Onan's death in Canaan as the basis for the tribe of Judah.
Supplements Genesis by identifying the mother of the first three sons.
Confirms that Shelah, Perez, and Serah became patriarchs of their respective clans.
Explains the origin of the last two sons (Perez and Serah) through Tamar.
Confirms Perez's sons Hezron and Hamul as links in the messianic lineage.
Alludes to the same lineage to establish Jesus' Jewish and messianic origins.
Supplements Genesis by identifying Hezron and Hamul as patriarchs of their own clans.
Uses the same lineage to trace Jesus' origin back to Judah.
